subject.title: Fork-per-issue from one warmed repo box

question: Should Clownfish adopt a warmed per-repo workspace backend for issue fan-out, and if so should it use mitos, a crabbox lease primitive, or a native workflow implementation?
rationale: The request changes runner architecture, workspace isolation, cache lifetime, and credential boundaries; source inspection shows no existing implementation path that can be safely completed as a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design opt-in lease backend first
options.body: Keep this open as architecture backlog and define the backend contract, isolation guarantees, rollout flag, and cleanup behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep current cached checkout model
options.body: Close or deprioritize the warmed-fork direction and continue improving ordinary target checkout and package-manager cache behavior.

options.title: Prototype one backend behind a flag
options.body: Allow a small experimental path only if maintainers accept temporary backend coupling and require proof on real bulk jobs before default use.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in lease backend first
recommendation.body: Keep this open as architecture backlog and define the backend contract, isolation guarantees, rollout flag, and cleanup behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the clearest recent history in the worker target-checkout and executor lifecycle that the architecture decision would touch.
